candidates.title: How a rainy afternoon in Montreal inspired an iconic Canadian board game
candidates.description: The bestselling Canadian board game of all time has sold more than 100 million copies worldwide, in 17 different languages. On the game's 45th anniversary, co-creator John Haney offers a personal account of the game's creation in his new book, My Trivial Pursuits: The Inside Story of the Board Game That Conquered the World.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: WhatsApp is a 'lifeline' for refugees. Advocates fear it could be severed in fight over federal bill
candidates.description: Meta said this week that Bill C-22 could force it to "consider" withdrawing encrypted services like WhatsApp from Canada. Rights advocates say that would cut refugees and other newcomers off from a key platform they rely on to get information and stay connected to relatives back home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A small latte and a chat, please: Why this B.C. café owner put conversation on the menu
candidates.description: Registered clinical counsellor Shane Trudell estimates one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but many people aren't aware of it. A New Westminster café hopes to help.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. couple lose business in devastating fire, credit volunteer firefighters with saving their home
candidates.description: A West Kootenay couple is counting their blessings after a massive fire destroyed their home-based mechanic shop in Burton, B.C. — and came dangerously close to taking their house with it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elite B.C. snowboarder's injury highlights financial strain of Olympic dreams
candidates.description: Prince George's Meryeta O'Dine suffered fractured ankle in a devastating crash during a snowboard cross training run in February and was unable to compete at the 2026 Olympics.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Will Canadian workers refuse to handle Israeli goods? Why unions increasingly say they should
candidates.description: A movement to cut off Israeli goods is spreading across Canada's unions. The Canadian Labour Congress, which represents more than 3 million workers, passed a resolution last month declaring trade, services and relationships with Israel to be “hot cargo," emphasizing a call for workers to refuse to handle weapons and military equipment destined for Israel.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Frustrated? Angry? Why these Nova Scotians say you should scream it out
candidates.description: A group of Nova Scotians now meet weekly to scream their frustrations into the ocean. From grocery prices to global instability, they say there's plenty to motivate them these days.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal police arrest 2 ex-officers for alleged assault, criminal harassment, breach of trust
candidates.description: The two officers had previously been placed on administrative leave and then fired from the Montreal police service. They were arrested after Quebec's Crown prosecutor's office issued a warrant.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Death outside Vancouver Island hospital raises questions about rural emergency care access
candidates.description: The death of a person outside the Port Hardy Hospital on northern Vancouver Island has renewed concerns about access to emergency care in rural B.C., where staffing shortages have forced some hospitals to close their emergency departments overnight.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman's airport security ordeal with dad's ashes highlights challenges of travelling with cremated remains
candidates.description: Rules around transporting creamated remains through airports and challenges with new scanners can add "another layer of grief" to an already stressful time, says the head of the Funeral Service Association of Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hudson, Que., community brings landmark church back to life after massive fire in 2024
candidates.description: More than two and a half years after a fire ripped through the historic St. James Church, work continues to bring it back to its former glory — but with a twist. The new space will serve not just as a church, but as a multipurpose community and cultural centre.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: City of Regina plans to shut down public transit starting Monday
candidates.description: ATU Canada president said workers have not had a new collective agreement for almost two years and the city chose to suspend services after the union said it would implement a ban on voluntary overtime starting Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Becky Druhan wins N.S. Liberal leadership, becomes first woman to lead party
candidates.description: Becky Druhan has defeated Amanda Mombourquette in a two-person race to become the first female leader of the Nova Scotia Liberals.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rohingya 'clearance operation' survivor in N.L. triumphant following genocide ruling
candidates.description: Muhammad Rofique of St. John's is celebrating, but still reflecting upon the atrocities he lived through in Myanmar as the world’s highest court declares the country committed genocide against his people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lawyers appeal nearly $500M cut to fees in historic $10B Robinson Huron Treaty settlement
candidates.description: Ontario’s top court heard an appeal Friday by the legal team behind the $10-billion Robinson Huron Treaty settlement — challenging a judge’s decision to slash their legal fees by nearly half a billion dollars.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge awards damages to both sides in lawsuit after neighbours' dispute over loose dogs 'spun out of control'
candidates.description: A judge has awarded an eastern Manitoba couple sued by their neighbour $10,000 in damages, and their neighbour $1,000, after an "unfortunate series of events" unfolded over dogs allowed to run loose on an unfenced property.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Satellites are constantly photographing Earth. A Waterloo student has compiled the pictures into one spot
candidates.description: Satellites are constantly photographing Earth, and a new website designed by a University of Waterloo student is making these public photos more accessible to the general public.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Age-Friendly initiative works to help Sask. seniors stay in their home communities
candidates.description: A program started by the World Health Organization is now developing in 16 locations across the province. Each community forms a committee that follows a template designed to address gaps in services available to older adults.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario Liberals elect Navdeep Bains as new party leader
candidates.description: Ontario Liberals have elected Navdeep Bains as the party's new leader after a marathon nine-month leadership race, with Bains emerging as victor less than one percentage point ahead of his next closest competitor, provincial caucus member Lee Fairclough.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why the U.S. midterms might have ended JD Vance's presidential hopes
candidates.description: Vice-President JD Vance's presidential ambitions for 2028 could be among the more significant political casualties of the Democratic blue wave in this month's midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: COP31 climate talks collapse after member states reject deal for not mentioning fossil fuels
candidates.description: Climate talks collapsed on Sunday at COP31 in Turkey, ending the longest ever UN climate summit with no deal to show for it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN-affiliated athlete swims in dangerous Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's impact on wildlife
candidates.description: Lewis Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days last week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how Iran war threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump calling Putin a friend is 'appalling,' says former ambassador to NATO
candidates.description: Kurt Volker, former U.S. Ambassador to NATO, tells CBC's Rosemary Barton that it’s 'appalling' to hear U.S. President Donald Trump double down on calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his 'friend.' Volker also weighs in on the leaked classified Pentagon memo about restricting defence ties with Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Fire at Indonesian candy factory leaves 3 dead, dozens of workers missing
candidates.description: A fire swept through a candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province Saturday, leaving three people dead and rescue teams searching for 36 workers who remained unaccounted for, officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN talks on AI in warfare end with no commitment to binding rules
candidates.description: UN-backed talks this week on regulating AI in warfare ended Saturday with nations agreeing to further discussion, but without a consensus on developing firm rules on how to rein in deadly autonomous weapons.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Capture of cartel leader in northern Mexico sets off gunfight that leaves 11 dead
candidates.description: A burst of violence in Mexico's Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, left at least 11 people dead, authorities said Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli settler violence at unprecedented levels during Palestinian olive harvest
candidates.description: There have been more settler attacks against Palestinians and their property during this year’s olive harvest than in 20 years of record-keeping by the United Nations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: FBI investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
candidates.description: The FBI is investigating a reported breach of its criminal information database, according to U.S. media reports. This is the second time the FBI has been the target of a cyberattack since September.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Elon Musk looks to break up with MAGA. To what end?
candidates.description: Elon Musk has certainly seemed to embrace the Make America Great Again movement. Why does that matter? Because the Tesla and Space X CEO now appears to be distancing himself.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Allies are buying Canadian underwater surveillance drones. Canada is 'not there yet'
candidates.description: Canada has a three-ocean coastline — 243,000 kilometres — and only 20 underwater drones to help defend it. The navy's commander confirms there isn't a solution ready a year after an internal document shows top officials talked about the need for a short-term fix.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine kills 2, wounds 60
candidates.description: A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza kills three, Gaza Health Ministry says
candidates.description: Israeli forces hit a truck in Gaza on Saturday that witnesses said was carrying food and papers bearing the logo of the World Central Kitchen charity, but the organization said the vehicle was not affiliated with it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Etsy faces backlash over including AI model training in new policy update
candidates.description: Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing products from the platform amid criticism for introducing AI model training as part of a policy change.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Quebecor CEO defends Telus bid, cites falling wireless prices and Canada's sovereignty
candidates.description: Quebecor CEO Pierre Karl Péladeau is defending his company's $31-billion bid to buy Telus amid concerns over competition in Canada's telecom sector, arguing the cost of wireless plans is dropping and non-Canadian companies are trying to expand.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bell says it's investigating cyberattack that led to potential theft of business customer data
candidates.description: Bell says it's investigating a cyber incident in which some enterprise client data may have been stolen. A spokesperson confirmed an "agentic" threat actor was able to access some of the company's systems, including one used for ordering and supplying telecommunication networks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
candidates.description: The talks fail to make a breakthrough on tackling climate change after a row about mentioning fossil fuels.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
candidates.description: The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
candidates.description: Libya's eastern government says the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
candidates.description: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
candidates.description: At least three people were killed and many more feared dead after a fire at a confectionary factory.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
candidates.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
candidates.description: The Army says "swift action" is necessary to protect its personnel and nearby communities around its ammunition plant in Iowa.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
candidates.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
candidates.description: The hair was given as a sign of friendship shortly before Washington's death in 1799, according to a descendent of its former owner.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
candidates.description: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
candidates.description: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
candidates.description: The Russian embassy in Denmark has denied the allegation, which has led to Russia's defence attaché being expelled.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: French police officers sentenced for beating of music producer Michel Zecler
candidates.description: The court has upheld the 2020 beating of the black music producer as an aggravated circumstance of racism.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
candidates.description: Pressures weighed on US markets, with the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed into correction territory.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, an Anthropic worker says he may have cracked the biggest
candidates.description: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used an AI to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis, though verification will take some time.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
candidates.description: Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it but delays arose over where to place inmates.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
candidates.description: Earlier this week, Trump greeted Putin ahead of a meeting in China and said the pair have a "great relationship".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US declassifies more UFO footage filmed in the Middle East
candidates.description: The Pentagon has released an eighth tranche of UFO records, which includes three video clips recorded in 2020, 2023 and 2026.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
candidates.description: When 16-year-old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl in an online game, it led to him and his mother helping the FBI rescue her from kidnapping.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
candidates.description: Fewer young people have registered to vote in next year's election than in 2023 - are young people losing faith in democracy?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: They were fined $811m for conning detained migrants, but the scams didn't stop
candidates.description: How convicted fraudsters made millions from detained immigrants, evaded efforts to shut down their bail business and left migrants behind bars.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
candidates.description: The ANC appears reluctant to replicate its national power-sharing deal with the pro-business DA at the local level.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: These dead pets were meant to be cremated - then their bodies appeared on a livestream
candidates.description: Grieving Filipinos confront a distressing reality: their dogs and cats may not have received the send-off they paid for.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Can AI really help spot Black Friday deals? We put it to the test
candidates.description: We put four AI models to the test to see if they could save us money on a new TV.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate summit?
candidates.description: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has formally come to an end after countries failed to agree a deal.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage
candidates.description: The mission is set to give us our best ever view of Mercury - the closest planet to the Sun.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at COP31 climate summit
candidates.description: The UN COP31 meeting in Turkey enters a second day of overtime as countries struggle to reach an agreement.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
candidates.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Birds killed in blaze at one of the largest foie gras farms in the US
candidates.description: Hundreds of young birds were also rescued from the fire, which comes as foie gras is under renewed scrutiny over animal welfare concerns.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex
candidates.description: There is now a self-sustaining population of the moth at a nature reserve in Essex, a charity says.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
candidates.description: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
candidates.description: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
candidates.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
candidates.description: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
candidates.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
candidates.description: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks
candidates.description: As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Phillips O'Brien of St. Andrew's University.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
candidates.description: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
candidates.description: Efforts to establish rules for AI-powered killer robots and drones have run aground. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva ended Saturday with an agreement to extend discussions for two more years.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare
candidates.description: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms
candidates.description: AI stocks — and the broader markets — got pummeled this week, raising major concerns about the financial system and the wider economy. Here's what to know.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
candidates.description: Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
candidates.description: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
candidates.description: South Africa is working to overcome a children's literacy crisis. In one Johannesburg township, a reading club is instilling a love of books in kids — and inspiring them to become authors.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
candidates.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
candidates.description: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Philadelphia neonatologist Joanna Parga-Belinkie on keeping babies safe from measles
candidates.description: Amid ongoing measles outbreaks, Philadelphia neonatologist Joanna Parga-Belinkie talks with NPR's Scott Simon about how she keeps infants too young for the vaccine safe.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.
